output.thorough_summary: Effective observation is the cornerstone of intelligence work. The ability to notice details that others miss distinguishes the professional operative from the amateur. This chapter explores the key techniques that enable observers to gather information without arousing suspicion. Casing is the practice of observing a location or person systematically. The operative develops a mental map of the environment, noting entrances, exits, and patterns of activity. This technique requires patience and deliberate attention. The operative should avoid staring. Instead, they use quick glances that capture details without drawing attention. The goal is to blend into the environment while maintaining awareness. Before observing, the operative must establish a baseline. The baseline is the normal pattern of activity in the environment. Deviations from the baseline indicate something worth investigating. For example, a person who arrives at a cafe every day at the same time is part of the baseline.
